assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes; daemon_capability: full; driver_capability: ready (keys ported, #1960 record pass)

## Reasoning

**The corpus-wide unknown is now resolved.** Every prior `decision_applied` record found across the 14-session muse corpus (muse-format-spec.md §5) had `decision_source.kind:"llm_judge"` — this environment's default `:auto-review` permission profile resolves every tool-approval request automatically via an LLM judge (`automated_review_started`/`automated_review_completed`), typically in 8-30s (real corpus example: `duration_ms:26096`). No human-decided example had ever been captured, so it was UNVERIFIED whether a genuinely human-blocking gate exists for muse at all.

I live-drove muse in a throwaway directory (`/private/tmp/.../scratchpad/muse-tgpp-live`, never inside the repo) with `muse --approval-judge off --approval-mode on-request` (both are real, documented top-level flags — `muse --help`: `--approval-judge <off|on> LLM approval judge for Prompt-bound calls (default: on)`) and asked it to run `rm -rf ./victim.txt`. The session (`01a09eea-4f5b-7933-b99a-8ae0ff158112`, this machine's `~/.local/share/muse/sessions/2026/09/14/`) opened a `kind:"approval"` `requested` record with `presentation_phase:"human_pending"` (NOT `"automated_reviewing"`, the value every llm_judge-path record carries) and `approval_wait.effect.started`, then sat genuinely idle for ~51s (sequence 103 at recorded_at 1789372585501461 -> sequence 106 at 1789372636449758) until I manually selected "Allow this stage once" in the TUI. The resulting `decision_applied` record carries **`decision_source:{"kind":"human_approval","action_digest":"sha256:f70db5d4..."}`** — a decision_source.kind literally never seen before in this column's research, confirming muse DOES support a genuine human-blocking permission gate, just not under its default profile. A new intermediate event kind, `stage_requirement_resolved`, also appeared per-stage before `decision_applied` (bookkeeping about a single requirement of a multi-stage command, not a second open/close pair).

**Daemon**: muse's adapter parser (`core/adapters/inbound/agents/muse/parser.go`, `parseApprovalEvent`/`parseApprovalRequested`/`parseApprovalDecisionApplied`) maps `kind:"approval"` `"requested"`/`"decision_applied"` to `ev.EventType = "permission_requested"`/`"permission_completed"` + `PermissionRequestIDs`/`PermissionResolvedIDs` UNCONDITIONALLY of `decision_source` — the parser never inspects who decided, only that a decision arrived. `core/pkg/tailer/tailer_metrics.go:656` folds these into `TranscriptPermissionPending = len(openPermissions) > 0`, and `core/application/services/state_classifier.go`'s `"transcript_permission_prompt"` rule (already proven live for GitHub Copilot, #1256) maps `TranscriptPermissionPending` to `StateWaiting`, ranked directly below the hook-tier permission rule and above every other transcript-tier rule — an open permission prompt always outranks `agent_done`. Because the mapping is decision_source-agnostic, the llm_judge path and the newly-confirmed human path are observed identically by the daemon: `daemon_capability=full` for both, no daemon work needed.

**Driver**: resolving the prompt in the TUI needs a bare, single, non-Enter keypress — I confirmed live that `tmux send-keys -t <session> "1"` (no trailing Enter) selects "Allow this stage once" immediately; the widget applies on keydown, unlike muse's OTHER first-run "trust this workspace" dialog, which explicitly needs `1` THEN `Enter` to confirm ("Use Up/Down or 1/2, then Enter.") and which the driver already dismisses cleanly via `--trust-workspace` at launch (no interactive step needed there at all). Sending a `send`-shaped "1"+Enter at the approval menu would submit a stray empty prompt once the Enter lands on the now-revealed, now-empty composer. `replaydata/agents/muse/driver-interactive.sh` DOES have a `keys)` case arm (line 671) but it is `not_implemented` and `keys` is absent from the `DRIVE_ELICITS` constant (line 167: `"send slash wait_turn sleep exit_clean restart sigkill start_session session"`) — confirmed via `tools/onboarding-factory/scripts/lib/recipe-lint.sh`'s semantic lint, which would flag this recipe's `keys` step as `not-elicited:keys` (a real `driver=ready (keys ported, #1960 record pass)`, not an observability limit). Separately, the driver also has no settings-driven wiring for `--approval-judge` yet (`MUSE_ARGS` currently only reads `.model`/`.base_url` from the settings blob per the existing `MODEL`/`BASE_URL` pattern at driver-interactive.sh:91-113) — `record` needs to add a third `.approval_judge -> --approval-judge <value>` arm, mechanically identical to the existing two.

## Why the recipe deliberately deviates from the default profile

Vacuous-pass check: under the DEFAULT profile (`--approval-judge on`, this environment's recorded default), the exact same recipe would ALSO produce a `waiting` episode — but resolved by an LLM judge in a bounded ~8-30s, never by a human. A cell recorded that way would pass while proving nothing about the scenario's actual claim ("user approves or denies") — it would be indistinguishable from re-recording the llm_judge path the corpus already has 11 examples of. `--approval-judge off` is therefore a LOAD-BEARING recipe precondition, not an incidental setting; see caveats.
caveats: LOAD-BEARING PRECONDITION: the recipe's `settings.approval_judge:"off"` is required for the wait to be genuinely human-decided. Under muse's default profile (--approval-judge on, this environment's recorded default for every other muse cell), the identical recipe would still enter `waiting` but resolve via the LLM judge in ~8-30s (decision_source.kind:"llm_judge") — a real but DIFFERENT flavor of this scenario, already well-represented in the corpus (muse-format-spec.md §5, testdata/real-approval-flow.jsonl). Re-probe this at record time: if the recorded decision_applied ever shows decision_source.kind other than "human_approval", the --approval-judge wiring did not reach the launched process and the cell is silently testing the wrong (llm_judge) path.

driver=gap:keys AND the driver has no settings-driven --approval-judge launch-arg wiring yet — both are real, small, mechanical driver additions record must port before this cell can run (see body). Neither is a daemon/architecture limit.

The scenario's claudecode-authored acceptance criteria include a 'late PostToolUse hook arriving after -> ready does NOT change state' variant. Muse is observe-only with no hook channel at all (muse-adapter-contract.md), so there is no out-of-band redelivery path to test; the closest analog is that the daemon's approval-request/resolve pairing is idempotent per pending_action_id (one requested/decision_applied pair per prompt in every corpus example, including this live probe), so a stale resolution cannot reopen `waiting`. This is architectural, not tested live — noted as a caveat rather than asserted as a spec phase.

muse spawns companion child sessions freely during any turn (muse-assess-context.md; also observed live here: two additional session ids, one nested under .../subagent/, one materializing as its own fully top-level session directory, likely a memory/goal-reminder agent). Every phase in the spec is pinned with same_session_as:session_birth to rule out the vacuous-pass mechanism the sibling cells 2-2 and 2-17 both hit and had to fix live (a subagent's own ready-adjacent arc silently satisfying an unpinned phase).

The model may add a self-directed 'double checking' pass after the tool call completes and before its final reply (observed live: a ~1m+ 'Double checking' span after the approval was granted) — timeout_seconds is set generously (240s) and the prompt explicitly discourages re-verification, but the exact working-span length before the final ready is not tightly pinned in the spec.

Not independently re-verified whether every stage of a multi-stage bash chain (rm/touch/echo in this recipe) gets the SAME per-stage safe/needs-approval classification as the live-tested rm/echo/ls chain — touch was not itself observed requiring or skipping approval. Low risk (all are common, harmless commands) but flagged as unconfirmed.

cost_nonzero must stay false: muse-spark-1.3-contributor has no pricing/alias entry (core/pkg/capacity), confirmed for every other muse cell in this onboarding pass — copied here rather than re-derived per-cell, per the established muse-wide fact.

RECORD-TIME FINDING (2026-09-14 recording, daemon 0.3.13+... branch build): the live daemon's events.jsonl for the primary session shows only ready->working->waiting->ready (seq 197/367/545/1291) -- the turn_resumed (waiting->working) phase never emits, so this cell committed known_failing (4/6 phases) rather than the full 5-transition arc the spec expects. This is NOT a fabricated permission resolution or a scenario mismatch: decision_source.kind=="human_approval" is confirmed for this run's decision_applied record (the load-bearing precondition held), and PERMISSION_GATE_OK landed as the final reply. Root-caused, not just observed: re-running the RAW recorded transcript through `go run ./tools/onboarding-factory/cmd/replay --adapter muse --debounce 0s <session.jsonl>` (event-by-event, no live debounce simulation) produces the FULL expected 5-transition arc -- ready->working(idx11 user_message)->waiting(idx66 permission_requested)->working(idx69 permission_completed)->ready(idx149 turn_done) -- proving the underlying transcript DOES carry a genuine, ~7.3s-wide working window between permission resolution and turn completion (muse-side recorded_at: decision_applied 2026-09-14T21:15:23.989754Z, run/terminal 2026-09-14T21:15:31.316483Z). The LIVE daemon simply never observed it: session_detector_activity.go's onActivity/processActivity re-reads the transcript's CURRENT state at each debounce-gated read (2s activityDebounceWindow, session_detector.go:33), and in this run's post-approval burst the daemon-side lifecycle log (147 transcript_activity/debounce_coalesced rows between seq 545 and 1291) never landed a read strictly between permission-resolved and turn-done -- so the classify pass that finally ran already saw both facts at once and jumped straight from waiting to ready. This is a genuine live-observability timing gap distinct from #1962 (shared-PID watched-map last-write-wins) and from the presession-identity-rekey shape in KNOWN_SEAMS.md -- both session ids and PIDs are correct throughout, only the intermediate STATE is missed. daemon_capability stays "full" (the underlying metrics computation is correct, per the debounce=0 replay) -- this is an observability-cadence caveat, not a capability downgrade, matching the precedent set by 2-21_streaming-partial-writes' known_failing verdict for a different last-write-wins race. Not filed as a GitHub issue per this pass's instructions; flagged here for the maintainer. A re-recording with a slower/chattier post-approval turn (more natural quiet gaps for the debounce to settle mid-turn) might reliably show the missing phase -- this was not re-attempted, so whether the gap is deterministic for this exact recipe shape or run-dependent is UNVERIFIED from a single recording.
